gaps.info: Precise dermatomal sensory testing (e.g., L4 vs L5 vs S1) to localize the affected nerve root
gaps.discriminates: L5 radiculopathy (lateral leg, dorsum of foot, great toe) vs S1 radiculopathy (posterior calf, lateral/sole of foot) — critical for correlating with MRI level and distinguishing from sacroiliac or hip referral

gaps.info: Assessment of Valsalva or cough-induced exacerbation of radicular pain
gaps.discriminates: Disc herniation (typically aggravated) vs acute lumbar strain or SI joint dysfunction (not typically Valsalva-sensitive)

gaps.info: Sacroiliac joint provocation tests (e.g., FABER, Gaenslen) and hip range-of-motion testing with reproduction of pain
gaps.discriminates: Sacroiliac joint dysfunction or hip pathology (which may mimic radicular pain but lack true neurologic signs and have negative SLR) vs disc herniation
